historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5y -2.2%, 3y 5.0%) diverges >30% from revenue (6.1%/3.3%) and EPS (26.4%/81.3%). Equity is distorted by EUR 3.5bn of buybacks in FY2021-22 and the Yeezy write-offs; EPS CAGRs start from the FY2020 COVID and FY2022 Yeezy troughs. Neither is a usable growth signal; revenue on the restated ex-Reebok basis is selected.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - lease principal - lease interest - SBC proxy), EUR m: FY2021 ~1,520, FY2022 ~-1,830, FY2023 ~1,320, FY2024 1,580, FY2025 -521. CAGRs are undefined (negative endpoints) and set null; the 5-year average (~EUR 415m, 1.8% of sales) is trough-laden and also not used as a base. Reported FCF 5y CAGR (934 -> 274) is -21.8%, driven by FY2025 inventory rebuild. SBC is immaterial (0.1-0.2% of sales), so the SBC adjustment does not change the growth picture; the lease adjustment (~EUR 750m/yr) does.

scenario_narratives.base: The Gulden turnaround holds but the lifestyle 'Terrace' cycle (Samba, Gazelle) normalizes, as the CEO himself flagged at Q3 2026. FY2026 lands on guidance (+9% reported revenue, ~EUR 2.5bn OP including a one-off ~EUR 200m tariff refund). FY2027 margin slips as the refund drops out and World Cup comps bite; Performance (running, football) and Greater China carry growth of 5-6% into FY2027-29, fading to the ~4% industry rate and 2.5%. EBITDA settles at a mid-cycle 13.5% (OP ~9%), short of management's double-digit target, because challenger brands (On, Hoka, New Balance, Anta) cap pricing power. Working capital stays at ~22% of sales.
scenario_narratives.bull: Performance credibility (Adizero marathon wins, football leadership, basketball) replaces lifestyle as the growth engine before Terrace fades, and share gains against a weakened Nike continue in China and North America. Management delivers its ~EUR 2bn/yr incremental revenue in FY2027-28 and reaches double-digit OP (EBITDA 15.5%, OP ~11%, the FY2018-19 peak) by FY2030 via DTC mix, full-price sell-through and SG&A leverage; a further ~EUR 300m of tariff refunds is upside not modelled.
scenario_narratives.bear: The lifestyle cycle breaks hard after the 2026 event year: industry-wide excess lifestyle inventory forces discounting, World Cup/Olympics demand proves non-recurring, and revenue stalls (~1% in FY2027-28) while US tariffs on Vietnam/Indonesia sourcing stay and refunds stop. OP falls back to ~6.5% (EBITDA 11%) -- roughly FY2024 levels, not the Yeezy trough -- as marketing spend to defend share stays high and own-retail deleverage lifts the lease burden to 3.2% of sales. Inventory ties up working capital at ~22% of sales.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF on a lease-consistent basis (lease cash charged in the flows, leases excluded from net debt). Neither the Yeezy trough (FY2022-23) nor the FY2025 working-capital-depressed FCF nor the FY2026 tariff-refund-flattered margin is capitalized; the terminal year carries a mid-cycle 13.5% EBITDA margin and a 15x cap appropriate to a fashion-cyclical consumer brand. Risk is charged once, in scenario flows and a 25% bear weight, with a single EUR WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Lifestyle footwear fade (Samba/Gazelle) faster than Performance can replace it
US tariff regime on Vietnam/Indonesia sourcing; refunds not guaranteed
Working-capital intensity: every 1pp of OWC/sales is ~EUR 250m of cash
Competitive erosion from On, Hoka, New Balance, Anta/Li Ning capping margins below the double-digit target
Key-person dependence on CEO Bjorn Gulden
Share count is an estimate (175.5m) pending the next disclosed figure; +/-0.5m shares is +/-0.3% of value

inputs.sbc_source: No SBC add-back exists in the adidas cash flow statement. Proxy = 'Repurchase of treasury shares due to share-based payments' (FY2025 AR cash flow statement line 18470: EUR 43m; FY2024 EUR 35m), i.e. gross cash spent buying shares for the employee stock purchase plan, Executive Board equity awards and third-party (athlete) equity awards. Deliberately conservative: EUR 39m of reissuance proceeds (employee contributions) is NOT netted. The cash-settled LTIP (the main executive incentive) is accrued in personnel expense and paid in cash, so it already sits inside EBITDA/OCF and needs no separate charge. Note 26 shows equity-settled employee-plan expense of only ~EUR 4.3m (FY2025). Net effect: SBC is immaterial (0.17% of sales) and house/street nearly coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: No buybacks FY2023-FY2025 (cash flow statement). FY2026: up to EUR 1bn announced, EUR 525m executed in H1 2026 (H1-2026 report line 358), shares cancelled (share capital EUR 179m -> 175m). The flat share count is therefore funded by a real repurchaser, but buybacks are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:39:04Z Xetra regular close (Friday); weekend, no after-hours print
inputs.share_count_basis: 175.5m: estimated shares outstanding at 30 June 2026. FY2025 AR shows 178,665,018; H1 2026 bought back EUR 525m (~2.9-3.2m shares at ~EUR 165-180) and share capital (EUR 1 par) fell from EUR 179m to EUR 175m. H1 report does not print the exact count; basic = diluted (no dilutive instruments, H1 2026 basic and diluted EPS both EUR 4.81). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The remaining ~EUR 475m of the 2026 programme (H2) is excluded on both sides (cash and shares) consistently.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-built. Risk-free 10y Bund ~2.7%, ERP 5.5%, levered beta ~1.05 -> cost of equity ~8.5%. Debt: A/A3 rated, ~3.5% pre-tax, ~2.6% after tax; capital weights at market: equity ~EUR 27.6bn, borrowings ~3.0bn + leases ~2.9bn (~18% debt). WACC ~7.4%, rounded UP to 8.0% to reflect fashion-cycle earnings volatility that the 15x terminal cap does not fully absorb. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and the lifestyle-fade risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not via scenario-specific discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. lease_cost_pct_path = lease principal + lease interest as % of revenue: FY2025 EUR 643m principal (CF statement line 18467) + EUR 109m interest on lease liabilities (lease note) = EUR 752m = 3.03% of sales (FY2024: 656 + 99 = 755, 3.19%). EBITDA (EUR 3,124m FY2025, company definition, post-IFRS 16) is therefore charged the full lease cash. da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 total D&A and impairment EUR 1,154m less ROU depreciation 639 + ROU impairment 26 = ~EUR 489m (2.0% of sales). Lease liabilities (EUR 2,929m at 30 June 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Net debt = short-term borrowings 560 + long-term borrowings 2,489 - cash 1,159 = EUR 1,890m (H1 2026 balance sheet).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%). NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at EUR 540m = FY2025 NCI net income EUR 45m x 12 (book NCI EUR 395m at 30 June 2026 understates the claim). NCI is ~3% of group net income.
inputs.notes:
MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, three scenarios (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). adidas is a global branded footwear/apparel operator with no lending, insurance or property-holding business; FCF is the right stream. No prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry: fresh build.

NORMALIZATION: FY2025 reported FCF (EUR 274m) is depressed by a EUR 2,043m working-capital outflow (inventories +1,104m to restock for growth); FY2022 and FY2023 are Yeezy-termination troughs (OP EUR 669m / 268m) and FY2020 is COVID. None is used as a steady-state base. The forward path is built from components and anchored to (i) FY2026 guidance (revenue +9-10% currency-neutral, OP ~EUR 2.5bn incl ~EUR 200m one-off US tariff refund), and (ii) a mid-cycle mature EBITDA margin of 13.5% (OP ~9%), below management's 'double-digit' OP ambition and below the FY2018-19 peak (~11% OP), above the decade average dragged down by COVID and Yeezy. FY2025 owner FCF on the lease-consistent basis was -EUR 521m (274 - 752 lease cash - 43 SBC); pre-working-capital it was ~EUR 1,519m (6.1% of sales), the better guide to run-rate cash generation. last_fcf (231 = 274 - 43 - 0) keeps the contract identity (reported - SBC - interest income) and is NOT lease-adjusted; leases enter the projection through lease_cost_pct_path.

INTEREST INCOME: OCF is stated before interest paid and interest received (both outside OCF), and EBITDA excludes interest income, so no deduction is needed; adidas is net-debt in any case.

WORKING CAPITAL: average operating working capital is guided at 22-23% of sales for FY2026 (FY2025 23.0%, H1 2026 24.0%); wc_capture -22% of the revenue increase (growth consumes cash).

REVENUE BASIS: FY2020 onward is restated ex-Reebok (divested 2021-22); historical CAGRs use FY2020+ continuing operations only.
inputs.fy2026_ytd_note: H1 2026 revenue EUR 13,335m (+10% reported), Q3 2026 EUR 7,252m (+9% reported) -> FY2026 year-1 growth of 9% reported is ~75% observed.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY2026 +9% reported (guidance 9-10% cn; H1 +10%, Q3 +9% reported). FY2027-28 near management's ~EUR 2bn/yr incremental revenue target (~7%) haircut for lifestyle normalization; fades toward industry ~4% then terminal.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2026: OP ~EUR 2.5bn guided (incl ~EUR 200m tariff refund) + ~EUR 1.15bn D&A on ~EUR 27bn sales = ~13.4%. FY2027 dips as the refund drops out and Samba/Gazelle normalizes. Mid-cycle 13.5% EBITDA (~9% OP) thereafter.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guided ~EUR 500m; historical (incl intangibles) 1.9-3.4% of sales; long-run 2.2% kept above D&A ex-ROU.
base.cash_tax_rationale: FY2025 ETR 24.3%, FY2024 26.5%; cash taxes paid EUR 399m on IBT 1,820 (22%). 25.5% long-run.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): the turnaround's most visible driver, the Terrace lifestyle franchise, is fading by management's own admission, fashion cycles have twice in a decade (Yeezy 2022-23, China 2021-22) cut OP by more than half, and US tariffs remain live. Base 50%: FY2026 is ~75% observed and on guidance. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs both Performance-led share gains AND a return to peak-cycle margins, two independent things going right in an industry Barclays sees growing ~4%/yr.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
